Q7401721.label: 1964 Saint Lucian general election
Q7401721.desc: General election results in Saint Lucia for 1964
Q7401721.summary: General elections were held in Saint Lucia on 25 June 1964. The result was a victory for the United Workers Party, which won six of the ten seats. Voter turnout was 51.8%.

Q7232761.label: 1949 Portuguese legislative election
Q7232761.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Portugal on 13 November 1949. Following the late withdrawal of the Democratic Opposition, only eight opposition candidates ran against the ruling National Union.

Q5602041.label: 1926 Greek presidential election
Q5602041.summary: Presidential elections were held in Greece between 4 and 11 April 1926. At the time the country was a dictatorship under Theodoros Pangalos, who had led a coup the previous year. Pangalos who was one of the two candidates; the other, Konstantinos Demertzis, withdrew from the contest before election day, but remained on the ballot paper. Pangalos received 93% of the vote. However, he was removed from office on 22 August following a counter-coup and was replaced by Pavlos Kountouriotis.

Q261881.label: 2008 Cypriot presidential election
Q261881.desc: 10th election of President of Cyprus Republic
Q261881.summary: Presidential elections were held in Cyprus on 17 February 2008, with a second round on 24 February. The second-round winner, and thus the President of Cyprus for the next term, was Dimitris Christofias.

Q1428217.label: Pro Patria Union
Q1428217.summary: The Pro Patria Union was a national-conservative political party in Estonia. The party was founded on 2 December 1995 from a merger of the Estonian National Independence Party and the Pro Patria National Coalition.

Q1046777.label: Progressive Party
Q1046777.summary: The Progressive Party is an agrarian political party in Iceland.

Q28055289.label: Assassination of Father Jerzy Popiełuszko
Q28055289.summary: On the night of 19 October 1984, 37-year-old Polish Catholic priest Jerzy Popiełuszko was attacked, kidnapped, and killed by three agents of the Polish Security Service, the communist counterintelligence agency in Polish People's Republic, who were disguised as traffic police.

Q16266489.label: 1999 Nigerien coup d'état
Q16266489.desc: military overthrow and assassination of Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara
Q16266489.summary: The 1999 Nigerien coup d'état occurred on 9 April 1999 and resulted in the death of President Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara and the installation of Daouda Malam Wanké as President on 11 April.

Q2665209.label: International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance
Q2665209.wiki: International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance
Q2665209.summary: The International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance (ICPPED) is an international human rights instrument of the United Nations intended to prevent forced disappearance, which, as defined in international law, is part of crimes against humanity.

Q3816697.label: Bombing of Barcelona
Q3816697.desc: 1938 bombing during the Spanish civil war
Q3816697.summary: The bombing of Barcelona was a series of airstrikes led by Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany supporting the Franco-led Nationalist rebel army, which took place from 16 to 18 March 1938, during the Spanish Civil War. Up to 1,300 people were killed and at least 2,000 were wounded.

Q140025.label: Japanese invasion of French Indochina
Q140025.summary: The Japanese invasion of French Indochina was a short undeclared military confrontation between Japan and Vichy France in northern French Indochina. Fighting lasted from 22 to 26 September 1940; the same time as the Battle of South Guangxi in the Sino-Japanese War, which was the main objective as to why Japan occupied Vietnam during this time.

Q460025.label: Italian participation in the Eastern Front
Q460025.wiki: Italian participation on the Eastern Front
Q460025.summary: The Italian participation on the Eastern Front represented the military intervention of the Kingdom of Italy in the Operation Barbarossa, launched by Nazi Germany against the Soviet Union in 1941. The commitment to actively take part in the German offensive was decided by Benito Mussolini a few months before the beginning of the operation, when he became aware of Adolf Hitler's intention to invade, but it was confirmed only on the morning of 22 June 1941, as soon as the Italian dictator was informed that same day the German armies had invaded the Soviet Union.

Q717561.label: Operation I-Go
Q717561.summary: Operation I-Go was an aerial counter-offensive launched by Imperial Japanese forces against Allied forces during the Solomon Islands and New Guinea campaigns in the Pacific Theater of World War II. Taking place from 1–16 April 1943, Japanese aircraft—primarily from Imperial Japanese Navy units under the command of Admirals Isoroku Yamamoto and Jinichi Kusaka—attacked Allied ships, aircraft, and land installations in the southeast Solomon Islands and New Guinea.

Q1330937.label: Operation Cockpit
Q1330937.desc: 1944 Allied raid on the Japanese-held island of Sabang
Q1330937.img: Sabang airfield under attack on 19 April 1944 (NNAM.1996.488.024.026).jpg
Q1330937.summary: Operation Cockpit was an Allied attack against the Japanese-held island of Sabang on 19 April 1944. It was conducted by aircraft flying from British and American aircraft carriers and targeted Japanese shipping and airfields. A small number of Japanese ships and aircraft were destroyed, and one American aircraft was lost. While the attack was successful tactically, it failed to divert Japanese forces from other areas as had been hoped.

Q111607033.label: attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
Q111607033.desc: attacks in western Russia during the invasion of Ukraine since 2022
Q111607033.wiki: Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)
Q111607033.summary: There have been attacks in mainland Russia as a result of the Russo-Ukrainian war since its invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022. The main targets have been the military, the arms industry and the oil industry. Many of the attacks have been drone strikes, firebombing, and rail sabotage. The Ukrainian intelligence services have acknowledged carrying out some of these attacks. Others have been carried out by anti-war activists in Russia. There have also been cross-border shelling, missile strikes, and covert raids from Ukraine, mainly in Belgorod, Kursk, and Bryansk oblasts.

mentions.c: Part of Russian invasion of Ukraine

Q112751353.label: Kremenchuk shopping mall attack
Q112751353.desc: 27 June 2022 attack during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
Q112751353.img: Shopping center in Kremenchuk after Russian shelling, 2022-06-27 (1) frame 0126.jpg
Q112751353.summary: On 27 June 2022, the Russian Armed Forces fired two Kh-22 cruise missiles into central Kremenchuk, Poltava Oblast, hitting the Kredmash road machinery plant and the immediately adjacent Amstor shopping mall. A fire broke out and the attack killed at least 20 people and injured at least 59. Russian media and officials carried conflicting stories about the attack.

Q315129.label: Oswald Avery
Q315129.desc: Canadian-born American physician and medical researcher
Q315129.summary: Oswald Theodore Avery Jr. was a Canadian-American physician and medical researcher. The major part of his career was spent at the Rockefeller Hospital in New York City. Avery was one of the first molecular biologists and a pioneer in immunochemistry, but he is best known for the experiment that isolated DNA as the material of which genes and chromosomes are made.

Q1321721.label: green liberalism
Q1321721.summary: Green liberalism, or liberal environmentalism, is liberalism that includes green politics in its ideology. Green liberals are usually liberal on social issues and "green" on economic issues. The term "green liberalism" was coined by political philosopher Marcel Wissenburg in his 1998 book Green Liberalism: The Free and The Green Society. He argues that liberalism must reject the idea of absolute property rights and accept restraints that limit the freedom to abuse nature and natural resources.

Q1627897.label: Horace Lamb
Q1627897.summary: Sir Horace Lamb was a British applied mathematician and author of several influential texts on classical physics, among them Hydrodynamics (1895) and Dynamical Theory of Sound (1910). Both of these books remain in print. The word vorticity was not coined by Lamb—it appears in English scientific literature as early as the 1880s, and the underlying mathematical concept was introduced by Hermann von Helmholtz in 1858—though Lamb's influential work helped to popularise the term in the English-speaking world.
